ReleaseRevisionPage.description: Session visibility is evaluated against durable original namespace/name/UID ownership. Every row cr_uid equals requested_cr_uid. Sort created_at DESC, revision DESC with cursor bound to query and authorization scope; do not promise frozen eligibility across pages. Replaced means the NAME has another UID; only old UID history is returned. Unknown means live K8s state unavailable, so is_active is last durable ledger observation and cannot prove current Callable. Store errors are 503, absence of verifiable visible history is 404, never synthesized empty success.

ReleaseRollbackEligibility.description: Read-time snapshot/reference eligibility, not a rollback success, runtime capacity reservation or Callable guarantee. Mutations recheck all gates. Closed reason codes belong to this draft version.

ReleaseRevisionSummary.description: Allowlist projection from retained original metadata; nullable when absent/not available. Never full spec, Secret ref/value, credentials, endpoint URL, command or Pod template.

secret.description: Only returned once. Never retry creation automatically.

RequestCapacityProjection.description: Readonly projection for original (slot_id, allocation_fence, request_id). Released requires matching release_log; held/quarantined require matching current allocation. A reused slot is not evidence. Reasons are sanitized existing release reason identifiers, not raw evidence. Release never implies refund, stopped engine or changed terminal/accounting.

RequestLookupEvidence.description: Not-admitted and expired require independently verifiable FINAL pre-admission rejection / retention marker for this exact ID within session visibility. They are optional evidence-backed capabilities, not requirements to create a second ledger. A missing row, UUID timestamp, current CR or 5xx is not proof. If only request rows exist, emit recorded or unknown.

RequestLookupPage.description: Exact mode only; every returned row ID MUST equal lookup.request_id and the query ID (cross-field equality is a semantic check). data_complete is completeness of this query observation, not finished generation, available usage or free capacity. Row and original allocation should be read in one primary consistent snapshot; otherwise checked_at timestamps must disclose separate observations.
